items.question: Do I need to rewrite my curriculum now?

children.text: The draft curriculum is for review and planning. Schools should continue to meet current statutory requirements until the new curriculum is confirmed.

items.question: Should I teach the draft curriculum?

children.text: Oak will update curriculum sequences and resources in stages as requirements are confirmed. This hub will make changes and timings clear.
Assessment arrangements will be updated separately by the responsible bodies. We will link to confirmed guidance when it is available.
The implementation date will be confirmed by the Department for Education. Until then, existing statutory requirements remain in force.

children.text: An overview of the proposed science curriculum changes for key stage 1.

modules.heading: What is changing in key stage 1 science?

children.text: The central scientific knowledge and practical enquiry expected in key stage 1 remain important foundations for the refreshed curriculum.
The refreshed key stage 1 content makes the intended progression and scientific practice more explicit.
New material is called out clearly so teachers can identify where additional planning may be needed.
Content no longer included in the proposal is identified separately from material that has moved.
Changes to sequence are explained so that their effect on prior and future learning can be reviewed.
Areas receiving greater emphasis are summarised with their implications for classroom practice.
Areas receiving less emphasis remain visible so that teachers can compare the proposal with their current curriculum.
Updated terms are listed alongside the language teachers and pupils may already know.
The revised sequence is summarised to show how knowledge and practice build through the key stage.

cells: Shared language helps pupils build knowledge
Teachers can plan across the key stage
Content is easier to apply in lessons
Checks can follow the intended progression

children.text: An overview of the proposed science curriculum changes for key stage 4.

modules.heading: What is changing in key stage 4 science?

children.text: The central scientific knowledge and practical enquiry expected in key stage 4 remain important foundations for the refreshed curriculum.
The refreshed key stage 4 content makes the intended progression and scientific practice more explicit.
New material is called out clearly so teachers can identify where additional planning may be needed.
Content no longer included in the proposal is identified separately from material that has moved.
Changes to sequence are explained so that their effect on prior and future learning can be reviewed.
Areas receiving greater emphasis are summarised with their implications for classroom practice.
Areas receiving less emphasis remain visible so that teachers can compare the proposal with their current curriculum.
Updated terms are listed alongside the language teachers and pupils may already know.
The revised sequence is summarised to show how knowledge and practice build through the key stage.

cells: Shared language helps pupils build knowledge
Teachers can plan across the key stage
Content is easier to apply in lessons
Checks can follow the intended progression

benefits: Practical leadership guidance from curriculum experts and school leaders

items.question: Do I need to rewrite my curriculum now?

children.text: The draft curriculum is for review and planning. Schools should continue to meet current statutory requirements until the new curriculum is confirmed.

items.question: Should I teach the draft curriculum?

children.text: Oak will update curriculum sequences and resources in stages as requirements are confirmed. This hub will make changes and timings clear.
Assessment arrangements will be updated separately by the responsible bodies. We will link to confirmed guidance when it is available.
The implementation date will be confirmed by the Department for Education. Until then, existing statutory requirements remain in force.
